title: Real-world post-deployment performance of a novel machine learning-based digital health technology for skin lesion assessment and suggestions for post-market surveillance.
summary: In prospective use at two NHS sites, DERM versions A/B were assessed across 14,500 cases; among 8,571 lesions with confirmed outcomes, reported melanoma sensitivity was 95–100% and malignancy sensitivity 96–100%, while benign specificity was 40.7–73.4%. Manufacturer ties, selection and differential-verification limitations constrain interpretation.
ai_technology: The DERM deep-ensemble image classifier analyzed dermoscopic images and returned lesion classes and referral recommendations; the paper evaluates its deployed performance.

evidence.tested: Among lesions with confirmed outcomes, the study reports melanoma sensitivity of 95–100%, malignancy sensitivity of 96–100%, benign specificity of 40.7–73.4%, and 15–31% eligible for discharge.
evidence.unknown: Prospective post-deployment pathways at University Hospitals Birmingham and West Suffolk (July 2021–October 2022), with histology/clinical references, second reads and repeat-presentation checks. Manufacturer employment/equity ties and selection and differential-verification limitations are reported.
evidence.ai_role: DERM returned lesion-class and referral recommendations during deployment; the study assessed real-world diagnostic performance against available clinical outcomes.

source_review.scope: Research Square v1 primary full text Methods/Results; version identity and first-posting date checked against primary version metadata.
